pr_title: br: Enable checkpoint advancer to pause tasks lagged too large
pr_body:
<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:

2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #50803

Problem Summary:

### What changed and how does it work?

Now, a new option called `CheckPointLagLimit` is added to the advancer config. When it is set, advancer will check if the checkpoint is lagged too large on every tick. If so, advancer would send a warning to PD and unstall the task.
PS: Theoretically, we need a resume signal when the task could be resumed. However, there is no channel to send this signal now. Maybe we will add it in the future.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
log backup block GC for a month.

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
below 6.5.6

review_comments: Nits: I think we'd better bring the default branch back and remove the `if`. Even in this context the `ctx` should be canceled and the channel must be closed. In a cleanup context, unbounded blocking is somehow dangerous -- it may lead to unexpected leakage or make the program fail to exit.
Would you also check whether the task has been paused?
It has been checked. When the task has been paused, `isPaused` field will be set and `tick` will run normally without error (for it is skipped).
It looks like an equivalent to `c.isPaused.Store(false)`.
Yes, they are equivalent. I just want to avoid to modify the value if redundant pause or resume signal are captured
I will prefer directly store a `false` when we don't need to keep the atomic semantic. But anyway, they are equivalent.
Note: we may unblock the GC immediately here. But this will make the task cannot be resumed any more. Perhaps we need a discussion about this.
